content_units: Option 1:   Knives Out   +   mini lemon bars   + The movie is sharp, witty, and full of bright twists, so a tangy handheld dessert matches its playful energy without feeling formal. The bite-size format also fits a clue-by-clue watch party mood.

Option 2:   See How They Run   +   jam thumbprint cookies   + This one has a theatrical, cheeky whodunit vibe, and the cookies feel equally lighthearted and a little old-fashioned in the best way. The little “center reveal” of jam also mirrors the fun of a mystery payoff.

Option 3:   The Afterparty   (pilot) +   build-your-own ice cream sundaes   + The pilot is energetic, funny, and built around competing versions of the same night, so an interactive dessert works perfectly. Let guests choose toppings while they trade theories.

Option 4:   Enola Holmes   +   chocolate chip cookie sandwiches   + It is clever, brisk, and puzzle-forward rather than grim, and cookie sandwiches keep the tone playful and crowd-friendly. They feel a little mischievous, which suits Enola’s style.

Option 5:   Only Murders in the Building   (pilot) +   cheesecake jars   + The pilot blends cozy mystery with charm and comedy, and individual cheesecake jars feel cute, casual, and easy to serve. They also suit a “everyone has a theory” living-room watch setup.
These fit your preferences especially well:
-   Coziest group pick:     Only Murders in the Building
-   Best if you want light mystery:     Enola Holmes
A few quick fit checks based on your preferences:
- The movie choices are broadly within your length preference and stay more clever than violent.
- The pilot picks are great if you want a lower-commitment start and easy conversation breaks between dessert servings.
